name: zzAT2_nav_click_probe

tests.name: the editor is the active application, so a pointer click can be routed at all

detail.note: THE PRECONDITION. Slate does not route pointer events into an inactive application, so a run taken while the editor is in the background measures focus, not the click path. The first run of this job failed all five tiles AND its own wallet control with app_active 0 and would have read as a product defect.

tests.name: the strip is on screen with nothing open over it

detail.note: every clause below is about a tile on this strip; if it is not up, nothing under it means anything.

tests.name: the wallet chip still completes a pointer click

detail.note: THE POSITIVE CONTROL, and it is the reason the two routes below can be compared at all. The wallet counts its clicks through an SButton OnClicked exactly as the tiles do and it passed in the same run that failed all six tile clauses. If it fails here, the pointer route is broken for everything and this run says nothing about the nav bar specifically.

tests.name: the tile button's own SimulateClick increments the counter for every tile

detail.note: WIRING ONLY. HandleClicked, Clicks[], the Id-to-index mapping and OnNavigate, with the pointer, the hit test and mouse capture all taken out of the question.

tests.name: a pointer click increments the counter for every tile

detail.note: the founder's actual route. This is the one that failed six clauses.
